# CP 219 (Machine Learning) — Project 1: Complete Project Summary

**Project Title**: Human vs. Machine Text Classification  
**Task**: Binary Classification on Obfuscated Token Sequences (`A` = Human, `B` = Machine)  
**Best Model**: `Tuned LightGBM with Combined Features` (Sparse TF-IDF + Extended Stylometric Features)  
**Peak 5-Fold Stratified CV Accuracy**: **92.61%**
**Final Best Submission**: Generated by `tune.py`

---

## 1. Executive Summary

This project addresses the challenge of identifying whether a sequence of tokens was authored by a human (`A`) or generated by a Large Language Model (`B`). All text in this dataset is anonymized/obfuscated into integer token IDs $\in [0, 18437]$ (where `0` denotes out-of-vocabulary / rare words). No raw text or external pre-trained LLM weights are accessible under competition constraints.

Through systematic iterations, we established a robust and clean pipeline:
1. **Initial Baselines (`train.py`)**: Token n-gram TF-IDF paired with linear models achieved **~90.19% CV accuracy**. Stylometry alone captured orthogonal signals, and stacking baselines into an out-of-fold meta-learner reached **~90.56%**.
2. **Extended Stylometry & Tuning (`tune.py`)**: By focusing on code stability and removing overly complex generative features that caused memory crashes, we expanded basic stylometry (adding positional head/tail stats, bigram entropy) and applied rigorous `RandomizedSearchCV` on LightGBM tree structures. This clean, robust model achieved our peak performance of **92.61% CV accuracy**.

---

## 2. Dataset & Problem Formulation

| Property | Value | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Training Set** | 10,536 documents | Labeled with class `A` (3,699, 35.1%) or `B` (6,837, 64.9%) |
| **Test Set** | 3,000 documents | Unlabeled, evaluated on 50% public / 50% private test split |
| **Class Imbalance** | Ratio B/A $\approx$ 1.848 | Handled via `scale_pos_weight = 1.848` and balanced class weights |
| **Vocabulary** | $V = 18,438$ tokens | Obfuscated token IDs $[0, 18437]$ |
| **Evaluation Metric**| Classification Accuracy | $\frac{\text{TP} + \text{TN}}{\text{Total}}$ |
| **Validation Protocol** | 5-Fold Stratified K-Fold | Seed 42, strict fold-by-fold fitting to prevent data leakage |

---

## 3. Iterative Modeling Progression

### Phase 1: Core Baselines (`train.py`)

We established the 4 required project baselines in a modular architecture:

* **Baseline 1 (BL1) — Lexical Token N-Grams (1–3 grams)**:
  - Vectorized whitespace-joined token sequences into sublinear-scaled TF-IDF (capped at 150,000 features).
  - Classifiers: SAGA Logistic Regression ($C=1.0$) and Isotonically Calibrated LinearSVC ($C=0.1$).
  - *Result*: **90.19% CV Accuracy** (LogReg), **89.85% CV Accuracy** (SVC).

* **Baseline 2 (BL2) — Handcrafted Statistical Stylometry (10 features)**:
  - Extracted dense macro-statistical metrics: Document length, Unique token count, Type-Token Ratio (TTR), OOV rate (token 0), Shannon entropy of token frequency, Mean and standard deviation of token IDs, Repetition rate (adjacent identical tokens), Maximum run length, and zlib compression ratio.
  - Classifiers: LightGBM and XGBoost trained with `scale_pos_weight = 1.848`.
  - *Result*: Stylometry alone proved fast and captured orthogonal properties of document composition.

* **Baseline 3 (BL3) — Sparse-Dense Feature Fusion**:
  - Combined the 150k sparse TF-IDF n-grams horizontally (`scipy.sparse.hstack`) with the 10 dense stylometric features.
  - Classifier: LightGBM.
  - *Result*: **90.07% CV Accuracy**, improving discrimination over either feature set alone.

* **Baseline 4 (BL4) — Out-of-Fold Stacking Meta-Ensemble**:
  - Stacked the out-of-fold probability vectors from BL1-LogReg, BL1-SVC, BL2-LGBM, BL2-XGB, and BL3-Combined.
  - Meta-learner: L-BFGS Logistic Regression ($C=1.0$) trained with balanced class weights.
  - *Result*: **90.56% CV Accuracy**; successfully reduced model variance.

---

### Phase 2: Extended Stylometry & Hyperparameter Tuning (`tune.py`)

To push past the 90.5% barrier without introducing unstable memory-heavy dependencies, we expanded stylometric features to 22 dimensions (`ExtendedStyleFeatures` in `src/features.py`):
- **Bigram Transition Dynamics**: Adjacent bigram Shannon entropy, unique bigram count, and bigram TTR.
- **Positional Signatures**: Mean token ID in opening 20 tokens vs. closing 20 tokens, and absolute head-tail divergence.
- **Frequency Concentration**: Top-1 relative frequency, top-5 cumulative frequency, and Hapax Legomena rate (fraction of singleton words).

**Hyperparameter Optimization**: Conducted `RandomizedSearchCV` on LightGBM tree structures (`num_leaves`, `min_child_samples`, `colsample_bytree`, `subsample`, `reg_alpha`, `reg_lambda`). 

**Result**: Combining the Extended Stylometry with the Tuned LightGBM yielded **92.61% CV Accuracy**.

---

## 4. Benchmark Performance Comparison

All models evaluated under identical 5-fold Stratified K-Fold CV (Seed 42):

| Model / Pipeline | Feature Set | CV Accuracy | CV ROC-AUC | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **BL1-SVC** | TF-IDF (1–3 gram, 150k) | 89.85% | 0.9610 | Linear Support Vector Classifier |
| **BL1-LogReg** | TF-IDF (1–3 gram, 150k) | 90.19% | 0.9652 | Logistic Regression |
| **BL2-LGBM** | 10 Stylometric Features | 81.42% | 0.8845 | Macro-statistical & compression properties |
| **BL3-Combined** | TF-IDF + 10 Stylometric | 90.07% | 0.9655 | Baseline Sparse-Dense stack |
| **BL4-Ensemble** | OOF Probability Stacking | 90.56% | 0.9646 | Meta Logistic Regression on base models |
| **Tuned-LGBM** *(Best)* | **TF-IDF + Extended Stylo** | **92.61%** | **0.97** | **Hyperparameter Tuned LightGBM + 22 Stylo Features** |

## 6. How to Reproduce & Submit

### 1. Reproducing the Best Model (92.61% CV)
To re-run the tuning pipeline and generate the best final submission:
```bash
python tune.py
```
This will:
- Extract TF-IDF + Extended Style Features.
- Apply the pre-calculated optimal LightGBM hyperparameters.
- Re-fit on the complete 10,536 training examples and output a submission CSV to `submissions/`.

### 2. Reproducing the Baselines
To re-run all 4 course baselines:
```bash
python train.py
```

## 7. Materials for Final Report & Bonus Mark Opportunity

In accordance with Section 5 of `Project1.md` ($\le 3$-page report guidelines and the 1 Bonus Mark opportunity):

1. **Bonus Mark Controlled Study**:
   - **Baseline (Without Idea)**: `BL3-Combined` (TF-IDF + standard stylometry with default LightGBM) $\to$ **90.07% CV Accuracy**.
   - **Proposed Method (With Idea)**: `tune.py` (Extended 22-dimension Stylometry + Hyperparameter Optimized LightGBM) $\to$ **92.61% CV Accuracy** (**+2.54% gain** under identical 5-fold CV protocol).
   - **Theoretical Justification**: Standard stylometry fails to capture positional token distributions and bigram transition entropy. Adding extended features like Head/Tail token divergence and Bigram Shannon Entropy provides the model with structural syntax hints. Pairing this with a randomized hyperparameter search prevented the LightGBM from overfitting on the sparse TF-IDF matrix (via tuned `min_child_samples` and `reg_lambda`), yielding a massive 2.5% generalization boost.
